question.problem: The arrivals of vehicles at a crossing occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of one every $10$ seconds. Determine the probability that the next vehicle will arrive at the crossing at least $5$ seconds after the previous vehicle's arrival. Round your answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Since arrivals of vehicles at the crossing occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next vehicle arrives as an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the amount of time between the arrival of two successive vehicles at the crossing. Then, since vehicles arrive every $10$ seconds on average, the rate is $\lambda =\frac{1}{10}$ vehicles per second.

The time between arrivals can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda =\frac{1}{10},$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{10}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10}{e}^{-x/10}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the next vehicle will arrive at the crossing at least $5$ seconds after the previous vehicle's arrival is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 5) & ={\int }_{5}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{5}^{\infty }\frac{1}{10}{e}^{-x/10}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x/10}{|}_{5}^{\infty } \\  & =-{e}^{-\infty }+{e}^{-5/10} \\  & =0+{e}^{-1/2} \\  & ={e}^{-1/2} \\  & ≈0.6065.\end{aligned}
$$
